decisions.transmission: t1 - free-to-air service, date not_stated, start time not_stated ('TRANSMISSION: not stated'). Decided as a conditional clearance over the whole clock rather than against a slot: branch A, any start before 21:00 or after 05:30; branch B, a start within 21:00-05:30.

classification.scheme: UK linear television issues no per-programme age rating; the BBFC 15 is evidence, not the answer

basis.why: The UK instrument is Ofcom's standards duty discharged through the Section One rules. Nothing in the slice creates a per-programme age label for linear television, so no number may be emitted here.

The Ofcom Code has in the main dispensed with the legacy link between a BBFC rating and the slot. The BBFC 15 recorded on this asset is a useful INDICATION of unsuitability for under-15s and feeds the evidence, but it does not set the classification or the hours. This is judgment_based and is relied on, which is one reason the decision is routed to a person.

hours.permitted: not before 21:00 and not after 05:30, i.e. within the 21:00-05:30 window only, subject to the conditions below
hours.without_technical_measure: 21:00-05:30 only. A start outside that window is barred on these observations.
hours.with_technical_measure: n/a on the facts given. UK-SCH-007 is the only instrument in the slice that opens the clock: it disapplies the watershed entirely while mandatory daytime protection is in place. The observations record access_control as not_stated on a service described as free-to-air, so no MDP is established and the unlock is not available. Branch, labelled: IF the transmitting service were under mandatory daytime protection, the watershed would cease to bind and the hours would be any time under UK-SCH-007; that branch is not taken here because nothing in the description supports it, and it must be confirmed rather than assumed.

basis.why: Representations of sexual intercourse must not occur before the watershed unless there is a SERIOUS EDUCATIONAL PURPOSE. The observation at 00:48:10 records that sexual intercourse is CLEARLY DEPICTED. No educational purpose of any kind is described - the scene is staged for comedy - so the higher bar is not met and the restriction bites before 21:00. This is the rule that places the hours, and it does so on the depiction, not on the certificate.

The watershed is 21:00-05:30, and material unsuitable for children should not in general be shown outside it. It supplies the upper boundary as well as the lower: the permitted window closes at 05:30, which UK-SEX-004 alone would not tell you.

Material broadcast AFTER the watershed containing strong or explicit sexual images, but which is not adult sex material, must be justified by the context. Clearly depicted intercourse is material of that kind, so clearance inside the window is conditional on contextual justification per UK-DEF-003 rather than automatic. The comedic, broad and unrealistic staging with no nudity and intercutting to reaction shots is material context pointing towards justification, but Rule 1.19 is judgment_based and the weighing is not this pipeline's to conclude.

other_restrictions.requirement: Any pre-transmission warning relied on to support the slot must be adequate, not merely present: its frequency and positioning must be sufficient for a feature-length programme, and it must convey the nature of what is coming rather than simply flag that something is present. The observations record warning_or_signposting as not_stated, so no mitigation can presently be credited to a warning.

basis.clause_ref: Bulletin issue 553, audience research cited in the decision

other_restrictions.requirement: A start at or shortly after 21:00 must observe a smooth transition: the programme must not open with its strongest material, and a programme crossing 21:00 must not abruptly become unsuitable. The single observation sits at 00:48:10 elapsed, so on the material supplied the film does not open on it; the event list is one entry for a feature with no runtime given, so this cannot be confirmed from the description. This condition sits ON TOP of the 21:00-05:30 window, not instead of it.

Any trailer or promo for this film is assessed in the slot it occupies and does not inherit the film's post-watershed permission. A trailer shown before 21:00 may contain only pre-watershed-appropriate material, which excludes the depiction at 00:48:10, and trailers of this kind should be kept away from children's and family programming and from content drawing a child audience such as live sport.

decisions.axis_note: The classification axis is empty and the hours axis is restrictive, and neither follows from the other. The hours are 21:00-05:30 because UK-SEX-004 bars representations of sexual intercourse before the watershed absent a serious educational purpose, which turns on what the observations record as depicted; they are NOT 21:00 because the film carries a BBFC 15, and a 15 certificate is evidence feeding UK-FLM-010 rather than a slot. The restrictions axis stacks rather than substitutes: UK-SCH-008's smooth-transition requirement is a condition ON TOP of the window (its time_rule_machine reads not_before=21:00;standard=smooth_transition, a window plus a requirement, which is cumulative), so a 21:05 start can satisfy every clock check and still breach. The one rule in the slice whose condition would SUBSTITUTE for the hours is UK-SCH-007, whose shape is any_time;override=watershed_disapplied_when_mdp_in_place; it is not available on a free-to-air service with no access control stated, and reporting 'any time' on its strength would be exactly the error of treating a condition as an unlock.
decisions.reasoning:
Routing. is_news_or_current_affairs is 'no', so the news carve-out does not apply. The description gives one transmission with no date and no start time, so no slot can be decided against; the decision is accordingly stated as a permitted window across the clock with the branches labelled, and the absent slot is recorded in missing_information rather than resolved by assumption. Service applicability: 'free-to-air' is stated, so UK-SCH-002 (free_to_air; all_linear_tv) and the all_linear_tv rows bind. The premium_subscription_film, pay_per_view and bbc_odps rows are out of scope for this service and were not in the slice.

Absolute prohibitions checked first, and read for what they cover rather than for their category labels. UK-SEX-001 (Rule 1.17) bars material equivalent to the BBFC R18 rating at any time, surviving every technical measure. The asset carries a BBFC 15 and the observation records clearly depicted intercourse with NO NUDITY, broad and unrealistic staging, scored for laughs and intercut with reaction shots. That is not R18-equivalent material, whose hallmark is explicit real sex for the primary purpose of sexual arousal, and applying UK-SEX-001 on the strength of its sexual_content label would refuse an ordinary post-watershed title. UK-FLM-006 (Rule 1.26) bars BBFC R18-rated films; this film is rated 15. UK-FLM-001 (Rule 1.22) bars films refused BBFC classification; this one was classified. UK-GEN-001 (Rule 1.1) bars material that might SERIOUSLY impair the development of under-eighteens, a deliberately higher bar than ordinary harm: a comedic sex scene with no nudity in a 15-rated comedy is harm-tier content at most, which is schedulable, not serious-impairment-tier content, which is not. No prohibition bites, so the decision proceeds.

The hours. UK-SEX-004 (Rule 1.20) is the operative rule and it is conditional rather than judgment_based: representations of sexual intercourse must not occur before the watershed unless there is a serious educational purpose. The condition is tested and fails - the description supports no educational purpose at all, the scene being staged for comedy - so the bar applies and the content cannot go out before 21:00. UK-SCH-002 (Rule 1.4) supplies the window's other edge at 05:30. Inside the window, UK-SEX-003 (Rule 1.19) requires strong or explicit sexual images that are not adult sex material to be justified by the context, context being defined by the eight factors in UK-DEF-003 including the time of broadcast, what is scheduled around it, the likely size and composition of the audience and the extent to which the content can be signalled in advance. The comedic and unrealistic framing, the absence of nudity and the intercutting to reaction shots all point towards justification, and UK-CTX-011 is the authority for the proposition that context can justify the content and still not justify the slot, so the two questions are kept apart. UK-SEX-003 is judgment_based and is relied on, which routes the decision to a person: the provisional view is that the scene is justifiable in a late-evening slot on these facts, and that view is explicitly provisional.

The ramp. UK-SCH-004 (Rule 1.6) and UK-SCH-008 (Rule 1.6 guidance) are the reason a 21:00 clearance is not the end of the matter: the watershed is a ramp, not a gate, and a programme commencing after the watershed must not open with its strongest material. The observations contain exactly one event, at 00:48:10 elapsed, with no runtime stated, so the material supplied neither confirms nor excludes a compliant ramp - and a single listed event for a feature-length BBFC 15 comedy is itself a reason to doubt that the event list is complete. UK-SCH-010 adds that audience composition before 21:00 is a gradient with the strongest expectation in the approach to 19:30, which is relevant only if an earlier slot were proposed, and that school holidays move the audience without moving the clock. UK-SCH-011 adds the cultural and religious calendar to the same effect. Both need the date, which is not stated.

Timeshift. UK-SCH-009 and UK-SCH-006 make a +1 showing its own decision in both directions: a 21:00 broadcast becomes 22:00 on a +1, but a 20:00 broadcast becomes 21:00, so the main-service time may need to move so that the +1 transmission still works for the audience it then reaches. No +1 is described; it is recorded as missing rather than assumed absent.

Nudity and music video. UK-NUD-001 (Rule 1.21) requires pre-watershed nudity to be context-justified; the second observation records expressly that no nudity is shown, so the rule is not engaged - and note that it would not have moved the hours in any event, since nudity is not automatically post-watershed. UK-MUS-002 concerns pre-watershed music videos and this is a comedy feature.

Certificate. UK-FLM-002 (Rule 1.23) bars BBFC 18-rated films before 21:00 on any service except under mandatory daytime protection; this film is rated 15, so the rule does not apply, and nothing should be read across from it. UK-FLM-010 governs the weight the 15 certificate carries: it is an indication of unsuitability for under-15s that supports the conclusion already reached on the depiction, not a substitute for it.

Conclusion. The hours are 21:00-05:30 on the rules supplied, placed by UK-SEX-004 and bounded by UK-SCH-002, conditional on contextual justification under UK-SEX-003 and on a smooth transition under UK-SCH-008/UK-SCH-004. Three of the rules relied on are judgment_based (UK-SEX-003, UK-SCH-008, UK-FLM-010, and UK-SCH-004), the intended slot and date are not stated, and the event list is one entry for a feature. The decision goes to a person.

rules_checked_not_triggered.why_not: Serious impairment of under-eighteens' development, prohibited absolutely. A comedic sex scene with no nudity in a 15-rated comedy is on the harm tier at most, not the seriously-impair tier.
Open-ended duty to take all reasonable steps to protect under-eighteens. Informs the reading of the operative rules; imposes no separate restriction.

R18-equivalent material, barred at any time. No nudity is shown, the staging is broad and unrealistic and scored for laughs; this is not explicit material whose primary purpose is sexual arousal. Read for what the rule covers, not for its sexual_content label.
Pre-watershed nudity must be context-justified. The description states expressly that no nudity is shown.
Pre-watershed music videos and inadequately covered performers. This is a comedy feature, not a music video.
Films refused BBFC classification. This film was classified, at 15.
BBFC 18-rated films before 21:00 absent mandatory daytime protection. The certificate is 15, so the rule does not apply and its MDP carve-out cannot be borrowed.
BBFC R18-rated films, barred entirely. The certificate is 15.

Appropriate scheduling of material unsuitable for children. It points the same way as UK-SEX-004 but is judgment_based and adds nothing the bright-line watershed and the Rule 1.20 bar do not already decide, so it is set aside rather than weighed.

Disapplies the watershed where mandatory daytime protection is in place. No access control is stated and the service is free-to-air, so the unlock is unavailable. Recorded as a labelled branch in hours.with_technical_measure and in missing_information, not as a basis.
Timeshift (+1) transmissions. None is described; recorded in missing_information because it would require its own decision and could force the main-service slot to move.
Specific care areas (family shows, soaps, daytime repeats edited for daytime). No daytime version or family-viewing placement is proposed; the +1 point is carried into missing_information.
The pre-21:00 audience gradient and the approach to 19:30. No pre-watershed slot is being sought, since UK-SEX-004 bars one; it would become central if an earlier slot were proposed.
The cultural and religious calendar raising the likely child audience within existing hours. The date is not stated, and the permitted window is already the late-evening one.
Audience and broadcaster size raise the contextual justification required and can never lower it. No channel is named; it can only tighten the UK-SEX-003 assessment a reviewer makes, never loosen it.

Offence and scheduling are determined separately. Applied in reading UK-SEX-003 so that contextual justification of the material is not mistaken for justification of the slot; it imposes nothing by itself.

'Children' means under-fifteens in the operative rules. Applied in reading UK-SCH-002 and UK-SEX-004; imposes nothing by itself. Worth noting against the BBFC 15, whose age matches the definition by coincidence rather than by operation.
Definition of appropriate scheduling. Applied in reading UK-SCH-001; imposes nothing by itself.
Definition of context (eight factors). Applied in reading UK-SEX-003; imposes nothing by itself.

Offensive language in programmes made for younger children. No language event is recorded, and the programme is not made for younger children. The absence of any language observation for a 15-rated comedy is flagged in missing_information.

review_reasons: UK-SEX-003 (Rule 1.19) is judgment_based and is relied on in the hours: whether clearly depicted intercourse is justified by the context inside the watershed window is a contextual weighing under UK-DEF-003, and the provisional view recorded here (that the comedic, non-nude, unrealistic staging supports justification) must be confirmed by a person.

UK-SCH-008 and UK-SCH-004 are judgment_based and impose a condition on top of the window: whether the film observes a smooth transition and does not open with its strongest material cannot be assessed from a one-event list with no runtime.
UK-FLM-010 is judgment_based and is relied on in the classification: how much weight the BBFC 15 carries as an indication is a judgement, and the certificate must not be allowed to become the answer.

The intended start time and date are not stated at all, so the decision is a conditional window rather than a clearance of a slot. A person must apply it to the actual slot, in particular to decide whether a start shortly after 21:00 satisfies UK-SCH-008.

One event is listed for a feature-length BBFC 15 comedy and no runtime is given. The description may be incomplete, and an incomplete event list is the one thing this pipeline cannot detect for itself.

missing_information.why_it_matters: 'TRANSMISSION: not stated'. Every clock rule in the slice (UK-SCH-002, UK-SEX-004, UK-SEX-003, UK-SCH-008, UK-SCH-010) is applied to a start time.
missing_information.what_changes_if_answered: A start inside 21:00-05:30 moves the question to contextual justification and the smooth transition; a start outside it is barred on these observations. A start shortly after 21:00 makes UK-SCH-008 decisive rather than cautionary.

missing_information.why_it_matters: UK-SCH-010 and UK-SCH-011 make school holidays and the cultural or religious calendar raise the expected child audience without moving the clock, and UK-DEF-002 lists school time, weekends and holidays among the scheduling factors.
missing_information.what_changes_if_answered: A school-holiday or festival date raises the contextual justification required under UK-SEX-003 within the same hours.

missing_information.field: whether mandatory daytime protection applies to the transmitting service (access_control)
missing_information.why_it_matters: UK-SCH-007 disapplies the watershed entirely while MDP is in place; it is the only rule in the slice that would substitute a technical measure for the hours.
missing_information.what_changes_if_answered: If MDP were in place the hours would be any time rather than 21:00-05:30. Nothing in the description supports it and the service is described as free-to-air, so the branch is labelled and not taken.

missing_information.field: total runtime and whether the event list is complete
missing_information.why_it_matters: UK-SCH-008 turns on where the strongest material sits relative to the start, and a single event at 00:48:10 in a feature with no stated runtime cannot establish that. UK-IMI-002 also makes assessment across a programme as a whole explicit.
missing_information.what_changes_if_answered: A complete event list could introduce language, violence or drug content that moves the hours later or engages rules not in this slice; it could equally confirm the ramp is compliant.

missing_information.field: whether any warning or signposting is given, and in what words
missing_information.why_it_matters: UK-WRN-002 and UK-WRN-003 govern whether a warning earns the mitigation claimed for it: it must be adequate in frequency and positioning and must convey severity rather than mere presence.
missing_information.what_changes_if_answered: An adequate warning is one of the main ways a broadcaster supports a borderline slot under UK-SEX-003. Recorded as not_stated, so no mitigation is currently credited.

missing_information.field: whether a +1 or other timeshift service carries this film
missing_information.why_it_matters: UK-SCH-009 and UK-SCH-006 make each showing its own decision, in both directions.
missing_information.what_changes_if_answered: A +1 showing needs a separate decision, and a main-service start at 20:00 would be inadmissible in its own right here while its +1 at 21:00 would not.

missing_information.field: whether any trailer or promo exists and in which breaks it is placed
missing_information.why_it_matters: UK-TRL-001, UK-TRL-002 and UK-TRL-003 assess a trailer in its own slot, with no inheritance from the feature.
missing_information.what_changes_if_answered: A pre-watershed trailer containing the 00:48:10 material would breach in its own right with no change to the film's decision.

missing_information.why_it_matters: UK-CTX-010 makes audience size part of the contextual justification required, and audience expectation for the channel at that time is one of the UK-DEF-003 context factors.
missing_information.what_changes_if_answered: A mainstream channel with popular appeal raises the justification required under UK-SEX-003; a niche channel does not lower it.

decisions.transmission: t1 - free-to-air service, i.e. a service other than a cinema channel or pay-per-view service, date not_stated, start time not_stated ('TRANSMISSION: not stated')

classification.value: III_-12 provisionally; II_-10 is not excluded and IV_-16 cannot be ruled out. The category is the editor's to assign and this is a branch, not a determination.
classification.scheme: French five-category scheme (I tous publics, II -10, III -12, IV -16, V -18), assigned by the editor through an internal commission de visionnage

basis.why: Category III (-12) covers cinematographic works banned to under-12s in cinemas AND programmes liable to DISTURB under-12s. Sexual intercourse clearly depicted on screen is material capable of disturbing under-12s even without nudity, which places the film provisionally at -12. The rule's other trigger, repeated physical or psychological violence, is absent. judgment_based and relied on, which routes this decision to a person.

Category II (-10) covers programmes certain scenes of which are liable to shock minors under 10. The scene clears this lower threshold on any reading, so II is the floor: the branch is between II and III (or higher), never I.

A cinema classification MAY SERVE AS AN INDICATION for the television classification, and the editor must verify that the rating transfers without harm and MAY STRENGTHEN IT - French practice being explicitly to raise the age limit between cinema and television, because a child who could not enter the cinema can easily be in front of a television set. The BBFC 15 is a UK cinema and video certificate, not a CNC visa, so it is an indication from another jurisdiction's scheme and not a French input; it points above -12 rather than below it, which is why IV (-16) cannot be ruled out. judgment_based reliance.

hours.permitted: Branch on the category, which is the editor's to assign. If III (-12): not before 22:00 on this service type, or after 20:30 only under the exceptional derogation and only on a permitted day and within the annual quota. If II (-10): no clock restriction, but the programme may not be placed within programmes intended for children. If the editor strengthens to IV (-16): not before 22:30.
hours.without_technical_measure: Same as above. France offers time and/or an appropriate technical process as alternatives, but no technical measure is available on a free-to-air service here and none is stated.
hours.with_technical_measure: n/a for categories II to IV on this service. The decoder-locking regime in the slice belongs to the category V (-18) scheme on cinema channels and pay-per-view services, which this is not; FR-CV-003 makes category V a total prohibition on a non-eligible service such as this one, so there is no technical measure that buys an earlier hour here.

basis.why: Category III (-12) on services OTHER THAN cinema channels and pay-per-view must not be broadcast before 22:00. This is bright_line and it is what places the hours on the provisional -12 branch; note it is 22:00 in France against 21:00 in the UK, a divergence driven by the rule and not by any difference in the content.

The exceptional derogation: category III may go out after 20:30 EXCEPT on Tuesdays, Fridays, Saturdays, the eve of public holidays and during school holidays, capped at 16 programmes a year of which at most 4 may be works banned to under-12s in cinemas. It is a permissive allowance and is reported for that reason, but its conditions cannot be verified: the broadcast date is not stated and an annual quota cannot be checked from a single asset description.

On the category II branch the timing is left to the editor's discretion with no clock restriction, subject only to the programme not being placed within programmes intended for children. This is why the French answer must be branched rather than stated: the same asset carries no clock restriction at II and a 22:00 floor at III.

Category IV (-16) on this service type may only be broadcast after 22:30, and there is no derogation equivalent to FR-SCH-004 for category IV. Reported because FR-FLM-001 makes strengthening above -12 a live possibility that the editor may reach.

The statutory hook: programmes liable to HARM minors must not be made available unless the choice of broadcast time AND any appropriate technical process ensure minors are not normally liable to see or hear them. Clearly depicted intercourse is harm-tier material, so one of the two instruments must be engaged; on a free-to-air service the available instrument is the hour.

other_restrictions.requirement: The category pictogram must remain on screen for the WHOLE DURATION of the programme (categories II to V).

A written mention must also appear: either at the bottom of the screen in white for at least 1 minute at the start, or full-screen before the programme for at least 12 seconds, worded 'deconseille aux moins de douze ans' on the -12 branch (or 'aux moins de dix ans' at II, 'aux moins de seize ans' at IV).
The classification must be made known to the public at the time of broadcast, in trailers, and in the programme schedules communicated to the press.

If the 20:30 derogation is used on the -12 branch, the broadcast must not fall on a Tuesday, Friday, Saturday, the eve of a public holiday or within French school holidays, must count against the 16-per-year cap (of which at most 4 may be works banned to under-12s in cinemas) and remains subject to the art. 1 violence conditions. The broadcast date is not stated and the annual quota is not auditable from this description, so the derogation cannot presently be relied on.

Any trailer must display the pictogram of the programme's category throughout and must not contain scenes likely to offend young viewers; on the -12 branch a trailer may not air close to children's programmes, and if the category were strengthened to -16 the trailer could not air before 20:30 - a trailer time distinct from the 22:30 programme time.

If the editor's commission were to classify the film in category V (-18), broadcast on this service would be totally prohibited, because a free-to-air service is not eligible under the -18 access-conditions regime. Nothing in the description puts the film at V - there is no nudity and no pornographic or degrading material - but the consequence is reported because the eligibility bar, not an hour, is what would apply.

decisions.axis_note: France issues a per-programme classification, so all three axes carry content here, and they do not predict one another. The classification is a branch (II / III / possibly IV) and the hours move with it in a way no rating-to-hours shortcut captures: at II there is NO clock restriction and only a placement bar (FR-SCH-001), at III a 22:00 floor (FR-SCH-002) with a conditional 20:30 derogation (FR-SCH-004), at IV a 22:30 floor with no derogation at all (FR-SCH-005). The restrictions axis stacks on top of whichever hour applies rather than replacing it: the pictogram and written mention (FR-SIG-001, FR-SIG-002) are owed at every category from II upward regardless of the hour. The only place a condition substitutes for an hour in the French slice is the category V decoder-locking regime, and that regime is unavailable here, where non-eligibility converts into a total prohibition (FR-CV-003) rather than into a later slot. Note also that the French trailer hour for -16 (20:30) is EARLIER than the -16 programme hour (22:30), which is the plainest demonstration in this table that the axes are independent.
decisions.reasoning:
Service applicability. The service is free-to-air, so it is a service other than a cinema channel or pay-per-view, which is exactly the scope of FR-SCH-002, FR-SCH-005 and FR-CV-003, and it is not eligible for the category V regime under the cinema-channel and pay-per-view rows, which were therefore outside the slice.

Absolute prohibitions checked first, read for what they cover and not for their labels. FR-LAW-001 (art. 15) bars programmes liable to SERIOUSLY harm (nuire gravement) minors' development, the higher of the two French tiers; nuire gravement is a deliberately higher bar than nuire, and a comedic sex scene with no nudity in a 15-rated comedy is tier-2 harm material, which is schedulable by choice of hour, not tier-1 material, which is not broadcastable at all. FR-PRO-002 (art. 3) bars PORNOGRAPHIC programmes DEPICTING UNDER-18s; it carries the sexual_content key and is retrieved by it, but what it covers is child pornography and it has nothing to say about a sex scene between adult characters in a comedy. Applying it on the strength of its label would refuse an ordinary post-watershed title, which is the specific error this step is warned against. FR-PRO-001 (art. 3) bars programmes offending human dignity, in particular those depicting sexual violence, perversions or degradation: the observation describes a consensual comic sex scene with no nudity, broad and unrealistic staging and intercutting to reaction shots, with nothing indicating violence, perversion or degradation, so the rule does not bite - though it is the one prohibition here whose assessment is a judgement rather than a reading, and a reviewer should confirm it against the actual scene. FR-PRO-003 (art. 3) bars extreme or gratuitous violence; none is observed. No prohibition bites.

Classification. This is where the French answer is made, and it is not made by this pipeline: FR-CLS-001 records that the editor classifies through an internal commission de visionnage. FR-CLS-002 sets the -10 floor (certain scenes liable to shock under-10s), which clearly depicted intercourse crosses. FR-CLS-003 sets -12 (liable to disturb under-12s, or banned to under-12s in cinemas); material of this kind is capable of disturbing under-12s even without nudity, so -12 is the provisional category. Above that the table gives no definitional threshold for category IV at all - FR-SCH-005 states the -16 hours but no row in the slice defines what makes a programme -16 - so the possibility of the editor strengthening to -16 can be flagged but not evaluated against a stated test. FR-FLM-001 both supplies the certificate's role and limits it: the cinema classification is an INDICATION which the editor must verify and may strengthen, French practice being to raise the age limit between cinema and television. Two things follow. First, the BBFC 15 is a UK certificate, not a CNC visa, so it is not the French input the rule contemplates; it is corroborative at most. Second, the direction of travel French practice prescribes is upward, so a 15 does not cap the French category at -12. The classification is therefore stated as a branch with a provisional value.

Hours, per branch. On the -12 branch FR-SCH-002 is bright_line: not before 22:00 on this service type. FR-SCH-004 is the permissive allowance and is reported as the procedure requires, because a system modelling only prohibitions over-restricts: after 20:30 is available, but not on Tuesdays, Fridays, Saturdays, the eve of a public holiday or during school holidays, capped at 16 programmes a year with at most 4 cinema -12 works. Its conditions cannot be verified here - the date is not stated, so the day-of-week and school-holiday exclusions cannot be checked, and an annual quota is a channel-level fact no asset description can carry. On the -10 branch FR-SCH-001 leaves the timing to the editor with no clock restriction, subject to the programme not being placed within children's programming. On a -16 branch FR-SCH-005 gives 22:30 with no derogation. FR-SCH-007 delegates the -18 hours entirely to Recommandation 2004-7, and on this service FR-CV-003 converts non-eligibility into a total prohibition; neither is reached on these facts but the -18 consequence is reported because it is a prohibition rather than a later hour.

Violence rules. FR-VIO-001 (art. 1) restricts violence, including psychological violence, between 06:00 and 22:00 where it could be perceived as continuous, as the only solution to conflicts or in an exacerbated form, and it is category-independent, so it can bite on a programme at any category. It is not engaged: no violence of any kind is observed. FR-VIO-002 (art. 1) is a derogation for historical or controversial subjects with educational support going beyond a warning; this is a comedy and the route is not available, which also means the general -12 hours cannot be softened by a warning. That the derogation expressly rejects a mere warning is worth stating, because a warning is the mitigation a broadcaster most often reaches for.

Signage. FR-SIG-001, FR-SIG-002 and FR-SIG-003 bind at every category from II upward, so on every branch except a category I the film carries the pictogram throughout, the written mention at the start and the classification in trailers and press schedules. These obligations are independent of the hour and are reported as restrictions rather than conditions of the hours.

Conclusion. The French answer is a branch because the classification is the editor's act and because the start time and date are both unstated. FR-CLS-003, FR-FLM-001, FR-PRO-001 and FR-VIO-001 are judgment_based; the first two are relied on. The decision goes to a person.

rules_checked_not_triggered.why_not: Absolute bar on programmes liable to SERIOUSLY harm (nuire gravement) minors' development. A comedic sex scene with no nudity is tier-2 harm material at most; treating nuire and nuire gravement as one tier would ban most of what the system exists to schedule.

Programmes offending human dignity, in particular sexual violence, perversions or degradation. The scene is consensual comic staging with no nudity; nothing in the description indicates violence, perversion or degradation. Flagged in review_reasons as the one prohibition whose assessment is a judgement.
Pornographic programmes depicting under-18s. Retrieved by its sexual_content key; what it bans is child pornography and it has nothing to say about a sex scene between adult characters in a comedy.
Extreme or gratuitous violence. No violence is observed.

Violence, including psychological violence, between 06:00 and 22:00 perceived as continuous, as the only solution to conflicts or in an exacerbated form. Category-independent, so it was tested on its own terms; no violence of any kind is observed.

Derogation permitting historical or controversial subjects before 22:00 with educational support beyond a warning. This is a comedy feature, so the route is unavailable; recorded because it also shows a warning alone cannot buy an earlier hour.

Category I (all audiences, no pictogram). Excluded: the scene crosses the category II threshold, so category I is unavailable. Cited here for the proposition that the editor classifies through its own commission de visionnage.

Total prohibition on category V on a service not eligible under the -18 regime. The service is indeed not eligible, but nothing puts the film at category V. Reported in other_restrictions for the consequence if the editor classified it there.
Delegates the category V hours to Recommandation 2004-7. Not reached; the film is not category V.
Procedure for revising a cinema visa at least 20 years old, by joint request of editor and producer. Not in point: there is no French visa to revise and no such request is described.

review_reasons: FR-CLS-003 is judgment_based and is relied on: whether clearly depicted intercourse is liable to DISTURB under-12s is the determination the whole French answer turns on, and the category is in any event the editor's to assign through its commission de visionnage (FR-CLS-001).

FR-FLM-001 is judgment_based and is relied on: the BBFC 15 is a foreign cinema and video certificate rather than a CNC visa, and French practice is expressly to STRENGTHEN the age limit between cinema and television, so whether the film sits at -12 or is raised to -16 is a judgement a person must make. The hours differ by 30 minutes between those two categories and the -16 branch has no derogation at all.

FR-PRO-001 (human dignity) is judgment_based. It is set aside on this description, but it is an absolute prohibition and the setting-aside rests on the description containing no indication of degradation; a reviewer should confirm that against the scene itself.

No start time and no date are stated, so the FR-SCH-004 derogation cannot be evaluated: its exclusions are day-of-week, public-holiday eve and French school holidays, and its 16-per-year cap with a 4-work sub-quota is a channel-level fact that no asset description can supply.

One event is listed for a feature-length comedy with no runtime given, so the classification is being made on what may be an incomplete event list. The French category is assigned to the programme as a whole.

missing_information.why_it_matters: FR-SCH-002 (22:00), FR-SCH-004 (after 20:30) and FR-SCH-005 (22:30) are all applied to a start time, and FR-VIO-001 runs a 06:00-22:00 window.
missing_information.what_changes_if_answered: A start at or after 22:00 clears the -12 branch outright; a start between 20:30 and 22:00 is admissible only under the derogation and only on a permitted day; a start before 20:30 is inadmissible on that branch.

missing_information.why_it_matters: FR-SCH-004 excludes Tuesdays, Fridays, Saturdays, the eve of public holidays and French school holidays. The description gives no date at all.
missing_information.what_changes_if_answered: The date decides whether the 20:30 derogation is available. Without it the derogation cannot be relied on and the floor stays at 22:00.

missing_information.field: the number of category III derogations already used this year, and of those, how many were cinema-banned-to-under-12s works
missing_information.why_it_matters: FR-SCH-004 caps the derogation at 16 programmes a year with a sub-quota of 4.
missing_information.what_changes_if_answered: If the quota is exhausted the derogation is unavailable regardless of the day, and the floor is 22:00.

missing_information.field: the category the editor's commission de visionnage actually assigns
missing_information.why_it_matters: Every French hour in the slice is keyed to the category, and the category is the editor's act under FR-CLS-001.
missing_information.what_changes_if_answered: II means no clock restriction with a placement bar; III means 22:00; IV means 22:30 with no derogation; V would mean total prohibition on this service under FR-CV-003.

missing_information.field: whether any French (CNC) classification or avertissement exists for this film
missing_information.why_it_matters: FR-CLS-003 brings a cinema interdiction to under-12s into at least category III, and per CSA practice a CNC avertissement classifies a film -12 for television. Only a BBFC certificate is recorded.
missing_information.what_changes_if_answered: A CNC -12 interdiction or avertissement would fix the floor at -12 as a matter of practice rather than judgement, removing much of the reason this decision escalates.

missing_information.field: total runtime and whether the event list is complete
missing_information.why_it_matters: The French category attaches to the programme as a whole, and FR-CLS-003's violence trigger turns on whether the programme resorts in a REPEATED way to physical or psychological violence - a question about the whole work, not one scene.
missing_information.what_changes_if_answered: Further events could raise the category, which would move both the hours and the signage wording.

missing_information.field: whether the programme would be placed within or adjacent to programmes intended for children
missing_information.why_it_matters: FR-SCH-001 bars a category II programme from being placed inside children's programming, and FR-TRL-002 keeps -12 trailers away from children's programmes.
missing_information.what_changes_if_answered: On the category II branch this placement bar is the ONLY restriction on timing, so it becomes the operative constraint.

missing_information.field: whether a trailer exists and where it is placed
missing_information.why_it_matters: FR-TRL-001 to FR-TRL-003 impose pictogram, content and placement obligations on trailers, with -16 trailers barred before 20:30.
missing_information.what_changes_if_answered: A trailer is its own compliance object with hours of its own that differ from the programme's.

cross_country_note: Both countries bar this film from daytime and both do so on the depiction rather than on the BBFC 15, but they diverge on the instrument, the hour and the signage, and the divergence is driven entirely by the rules rather than by any difference in the content. The UK issues no per-programme rating and sets a 21:00-05:30 window, placed by UK-SEX-004's bar on representations of sexual intercourse before the watershed and bounded above by UK-SCH-002; France issues a per-programme category and, on the provisional -12 branch, sets a 22:00 floor under FR-SCH-002 - an hour later than the UK, with a conditional 20:30 derogation (FR-SCH-004) that has no UK counterpart and that the UK watershed would never permit. The certificate is treated similarly in form and differently in direction: UK-FLM-010 makes it an indication that does not set the slot, while FR-FLM-001 makes it an indication the editor may STRENGTHEN, with French practice being expressly to raise the age limit between cinema and television - so the same 15 pulls the French answer upward in a way it does not pull the UK answer. France also imposes obligations the UK does not: a pictogram for the whole duration, a written mention at the start and publication of the classification in trailers and press schedules (FR-SIG-001 to FR-SIG-003), none of which has a UK equivalent in this slice. One asymmetry is worth naming: the UK slice has an unlock that France does not offer on this service, in UK-SCH-007's disapplication of the watershed under mandatory daytime protection, while in France non-eligibility for the only access-controlled regime converts into a total prohibition (FR-CV-003) rather than into a later hour. Both decisions escalate, for related but distinct reasons: in the UK the judgement is the contextual justification of an admittedly post-watershed scene (UK-SEX-003); in France the judgement is the category itself (FR-CLS-003, FR-FLM-001), and the category is in any case the editor's own act. Both are hampered by the same two gaps in the description - no start time, no date - and by one event listed for a feature-length film with no runtime.
